subject: LLM sourcing assessment - next steps & compatibility notes
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Chen <maya@medintel.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@medintel.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: LLM sourcing assessment - notes & next steps

Thanks for your time this morning — good conversation. Below is a concise recap of what we heard on the call, the success criteria you described, and suggested next steps so the team has a single source of truth. Happy to adjust if I missed anything.

Summary of pain points (as stated by MedIntel):
- Cost volatility with current OpenAI usage at scale; embedding/embedding-search costs are a major line item.
- Rate limits and queueing: spikes in usage during overnight processing create throttling and retries.
- Data residency / PHI concerns: certain logs & prompt/response pairs must stay inside a HIPAA-compliant boundary.
- Inconsistent output behavior between model variants (in particular, hallucination on certain clinical templates).

Current stack (clarified on call):
- Primary generation: OpenAI GPT-4 family for clinical summarization and patient Q&A.
- Secondary: Anthropic Claude for longer-form summarization experiments.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings (1536-d) powering semantic search.
- Orchestration: mix of serverless endpoints + a small on-prem batch pipeline for nightly jobs.

Success criteria for a viable open-model migration (your checklist):
- Maintain or improve summary accuracy on existing evals (target: F1/composite >= current baseline).
- Embeddings parity (1536-d, similar nearest-neighbor recall at top-10).
- Production p95 latency <= 500ms for 2k prompt + 256 generation on dedicated infra.
- Cost per 1k-generation tokens <= $0.002 (target, inclusive of infra amortization).
- HIPAA controls: audit logs, KMS integration, and optional on-prem/private deployment.

Compatibility requirements you emphasized:
- Tool/function-calling parity (we heard you rely on function-style structured outputs).
- Streaming response capability for the live chat flows.
- Deterministic seeding for a set of offline batch jobs.
- Tokenization differences: minimal drift for existing prompt templates.

Initial model shortlist (for technical validation / POC):
- Llama-2-Chat variants (13B/70B quantized) — strong in instruction tuning for chat.
- Mistral Instruct (mid-size) — low-latency, promising cost profile.
- Falcon-40B-instruct (float/quantized) — strong generation quality on long-form clinical text.
- RedPajama family (chat-tuned checkpoint) — candidate for embeddings and cheaper instantiation.

Proposed next steps (high priority):
1) Security questionnaire: we attached an initial spreadsheet (MedIntel_Security_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx). Please flag any items you want us to pre-populate.
2) POC scope: Redwood will provision a short POC (2-week) that evaluates 2 models from the shortlist on your eval set.
   - We need: a representative set of 100 prompts (send as medintel_eval_prompts.csv) + 3 weeks of recent anonymized logs if possible.
3) Technical workshop: 60-minute working session with your infra/security (suggest Aug 4 or Aug 6).
4) Cost & capacity estimate: we'll follow up with a Dedicated vs Hosted cost delta once we confirm model choices and target throughput.
5) NDA/Docs: link to a one-click DocuSign for an NDA if you prefer (I included a link below).

Immediate asks for MedIntel (action items):
- Share medintel_eval_prompts.csv (sample prompt set) and a short list of 10 queries where hallucination is highest.
- Confirm whether PHI will be present in prompts/responses for the POC (yes/no).
- Point of contact for security questionnaire (we heard Raj + security@medintel.com).

Attachments included: MedIntel_Security_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx, medintel_eval_prompts.csv (blank template).

If this all looks correct I can send a formal POC SOW and proposed schedule by end of day Monday. Thanks again — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medintel.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Chen <maya@medintel.com>
Cc: security@medintel.com
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 12:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: LLM sourcing assessment - notes & next steps

Thanks Jordan — this is a great recap and captures the main points. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Embedding dimension: the production system expects 1536-d vectors for backwards compatibility with our semantic index. Any embedding candidate must match or have a clear migration path.
- Tool calling: our triage layer relies on structured JSON outputs from the model (intent + arguments). We need an integration that preserves that shape without heavy post-processing.
- Streaming: for the live clinician chat we stream tokens as they are generated; buffering strategies that add >300ms are problematic.
- Compliance: PHI will appear in a subset of prompts; we need an architecture that either keeps PHI in our VPC or uses customer-managed keys.

Requests: 
1) Please include in the POC two embedding candidates: (a) an open-embedding that matches 1536-d or (b) a conversion path with mapping documentation.
2) Can you provide 1-2 references of healthcare customers that have moved portions of their stack to open models (anonymized if needed)?
3) Timing: we can do the workshop week of Aug 2; prefer Aug 4 afternoon CT.

We'll upload an initial redacted log bundle by Monday. Thanks — Raj

--
Raj Patel
VP Product, MedIntel
raj.patel@medintel.com | +1 (212) 555-0199
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medintel.com>, Maya Chen <maya@medintel.com>

Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 13:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LLM sourcing assessment - notes & next steps

Appreciate the clarifications, Raj — those are all doable. Quick responses inline: 

- Embeddings: we'll include an OpenAI-compatible 1536-d embedding candidate (model conversion + normalization) and a native open-embedding from the RedPajama family; we'll include recall/precision comparisons in the POC report.
- Tool-calling: we'll prototype a function-output shim that preserves your JSON schema; if needed, we can run a lightweight adapter in your VPC during the POC.
- Streaming latency: Redwood's hosted runtime supports streaming; for Dedicated we can guarantee sub-300ms token emission for small batches — we'll validate during POC.
- PHI/Key management: we support customer KMS and on-prem/private deployment for the sensitive workloads.

Next items from our side: 
- I'll send the POC SOW & schedule Monday (includes model pairs, test harness, and evaluation rubric).
- DocuSign NDA link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abcd-ef12-3456 (feel free to route internally).

Proposed POC timeline (high level):
- Week 0: NDA + scope finalization + sample artifacts (you)
- Week 1: Redwood provisions models + baseline runs against your eval set
- Week 2: Joint analysis & tweak runs; final POC report end of week 2

Can you confirm: (a) Aug 4 afternoon CT for the workshop, (b) whether PHI will be included in the redacted upload (yes/no), and (c) a short list of which two models you'd like us to prioritize from the shortlist?

I'll also attach a lightweight SOW stub in my follow-up. Thanks, Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: LLM sourcing assessment - internal pricing note

FW: quick note for the deal file (RED-1983) — putting an early estimate here so we can move fast once MedIntel confirms POC models. Numbers are rough until we size throughput: 

- Hosted POC (two models, low throughput): $8k flat (covers infra + evaluation + 2-week support).
- Dedicated evaluation (reserve 1 GPU pool with autoscale): ~$18k one-time setup + monthly run-rate (depends on GPU class) — include customer-managed KMS option.
- Discount: propose standard enterprise 15% off first 6 months if committed to Dedicated within 60 days.

I'll draft a short SOW template to attach to Jordan's Monday note. Also adding the security questionnaire to the deal in HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/RED-1983
